title: No Verified Case Means No Honest Raid Narrative
excerpt: No court record, police seizure, or intercepted shipment appears here. Claims about stolen pets and dog-meat networks need documented evidence before publication.
body_html:
No verified raid, arrest, court verdict, or intercepted shipment is documented in the supplied material. That leaves families, animals, and readers without facts strong enough to name a case, identify defendants, or describe stolen companions without risking invention.

Evidence must carry accusation

Pet theft, poison bait, illegal transport, forged quarantine papers, and cruelty demand precise records: date, location, agency, case status, seized animals, and source URL. None is supplied here. Anger cannot replace evidence. Vietnamese families defending pets deserve reporting that names proven violations, not scenes built from assumptions.

Biosecurity needs accurate facts

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance supports these medical facts.

Household exposure incidents and commercial animal-trade risks must remain distinct. Both demand strong prevention, inspection, quarantine, and enforcement. The SDE campaign calls for nationwide abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030; that is a policy demand, not a claim that one petition instantly ends enforcement failures.

Document first. Demand change.

Verified police, court, veterinary, and health records can turn public concern into accountable action. Sign the national petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Add your name to a public demand for action and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.

Claims about poison bait, illegal transport, forged quarantine papers, and stolen pets need records that Vietnamese families, journalists, and officials can check.

Public safety still demands clear facts. Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies must come before symptoms. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Commercial dog-meat supply chains and household exposure incidents remain separate issues, but both require serious prevention and enforcement.
